To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have purified and characterized a calcium-activated neutral protease (CANP or calpain) from myelin of the central nervous system.

we purified a calcium-activated neutral protease (CANP, also called calpain) from myelin of the bovine brain white mater, that the myelin CANP was activated by TritonX100, that the purified enzyme was a single subunit of 70–75 K, that it required Ca2+ and was inhibited by calpastatin, and that it may mediate the turn over of myelin proteins.
we purified CANP from myelin and that the purified enzyme has a major subunit in the range of 72-76 K.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the purification of a calcium-activated neutral protease (CANP), which has been purified to homogeneity from bovine white matter.
the isolation, characterization and purification of CANP in bovine brain myelin.
understanding the mechanism of CANP in the pathogenesis of multiple sclerosis and Alzheimer’s disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CANP is a Ca2+-dependent protease which is involved in the degradation of myelin proteins in myelin breakdown.

the CANP purified from bovine brain white myelin is a 72–76 kDa protein that is activated by 5 mM CaCl2 and 0.5 mM MnCl2, and that is inhibited by iodoacetic acid, leupeptin, E-64, antipain, calpastatin and ZnCl2, but not by Mg2+.
this is a novel calcium-activated neutral protease from myelin of the bovine brain white mater.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have purified CANP from bovine brain myelin.
we have purified a Ca2+-activated neutral protease from myelin.
the CANP purified from myelin has a similar biochemical and enzymological properties as that of the CANP purified previously from other brain tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CANP activity is increased in the myelin of the brains from Alzheimer patients.
CANP may play an important role in myelin degradation and turnover.
the enzyme is present in the myelin and is activated by calcium.
